intro.text: eylem eylül acarsoy. eylosh, for short.
a researcher and designer who never managed to stay in one discipline.
she is curious about how identity, expression and introspection are shaped by the societies and institutions around us.
she studied visual communication design with a strong dose of cultural studies, and spent a few years in sociology too. one taught her to make things, the other to ask why people do what they do.
she has run cultural and educational spaces and organisations, coordinated projects and events, facilitated workshops, built archives, and gave art, research and organisations a visual voice.
today she is a master's candidate in the social and public innovation cluster at KISD in cologne, and a research assistant at the university of wuppertal.
she looks at things from six sides:
intro.then: she loves solutions, but she doesn't rush them.

intro.text: she feels most at home in community. these days that's the hidden agenda collective: artists and designers from many fields.
also: her family's home is a sanctuary for adopted stray cats. nine of them, currently.
there are several versions of her. choose one.

works.title: the]institute]of[inner[mechanics
works.question: What would an institute dedicated to introspection look like?
works.text: Investigates inner capacity as a regenerative capacity within creative education. Through a fictional institute, it combines theoretical research, interviews, autoethnography, speculative storytelling, participatory workshops and visual mapping. Two modules: The Playground of Inner Things (with Diego Alatorre Guzmán), participatory workshops using the storytelling game Feely Thingies; and The Bureau of Inner Economies (with Oliver Baron), interviews with alternative education models. The institute is fictional; the experiences and research processes informing it are real.
works.role: Research, concept development, speculative world-building, visual identity, participatory methods
works.context_line: Master's thesis at KISD, TH Köln: a fictional institute built on real workshops and research.

credits.with: supervised by Prof. Oliver Baron & Diego Alatorre Guzmán

works.title: Refin(d)ing KISD
works.question: What makes a design school feel like a place where you belong?
works.text: Explores how students experience design education at KISD through surveys, conversations, collective reflection and a doll-making workshop: designer identity, learning habits, uncertainty, autonomy and community.
works.context_line: A collective research project at KISD on how design education actually feels from the inside.

works.title: BAYETAV Art
works.question: How can a cultural space create opportunities for encounter and exchange?
works.text: Coordinated exhibitions (Yeryüzüne Övgü, Kendisinden doğup kendisine dönen, Mahsul Vakaları) and a public programme of workshops, concerts, talks and screenings. Strategic planning, workflows, venue manual, people management.
works.role: Design & experience strategist · strategic planning · exhibition & event coordination · people & project management
works.context_line: Two years inside a cultural foundation's art space: exhibitions, public programmes and the workflows behind them.

review.text: BAYETAV's transdisciplinary structure is the ultimate space for me today. Traces of my portfolio projects can be found in every task I tackle here, and I've advanced ongoing projects by incorporating innovation gleaned from my other works' shortcomings.

works.title: İHKİB GİY
works.question: How can design education bring different disciplines together to rethink fashion?
works.text: An apparel innovation and education platform for university students. Visual identity, learning materials (road-map booklet, empathy map, idea assessment matrix, jury manual), design-thinking workshops, mentoring and programme coordination.
works.context_line: An apparel innovation competition and education platform by İHKİB for university students from all disciplines.

review.text: GİY was my first project that reinforced an empathy-driven approach and taught me to deal with uncertainty. As a recent graduate, I emphasized a student-centric approach, highlighting education and the student experience, which fueled my curiosity in education.

works.title: Motif
works.tag: Critical Design · Tangible Interaction · Graduation Project
works.question: What happens when a society gets stuck in its search for originality?
works.text: A tangible interactive storytelling console. Placing physical tools into slots on a 3D island model reveals fragments of a non-linear story about originality, consumerism, ego and mimetic theory.
works.role: Concept · storytelling · interaction design · tangible prototyping · installation
works.tools: Arduino · Processing · 3D printing · laser-cut cardboard · projection mapping
works.context_line: Graduation project at Yaşar University, shown at Good Design ÜTAŞ 2021.

review.text: I engaged in philosophical debates about Motif's nature, leading me towards critical design. The project contained compelling elements of system design, nudging me towards service design within its narrative. My presentation of Motif was methodological, systematic, and comprehensive.

works.question: How might people experience a city beyond what they can see?
works.text: A mobile experience designed for and with visually impaired and blind people, turning textures into sound and guiding them through cultural and historical places. With İzmir Tarih, İzmir Municipality and Vestel's UX team.
works.role: Team project (with Merve Topay, Zeynep Güneş Acar)
works.context_line: A team project with İzmir Tarih, İzmir Municipality and Vestel's UX team.

credits.with: with Merve Topay & Zeynep Güneş Acar

review.text: In this project, insightful interviews combined with our research led to a strong application. However, our presentation lacked impact in conveying the discussed technology. Given another chance, I would research and prototype the technology earlier to enhance the presentation's effectiveness.

works.title: Customer Centers of the Future
works.question: How do people feel about bureaucracy before they even arrive?
works.text: A team project with the City of Cologne, researching and redesigning services for the Kundenzentrum. The research focused on the digital appointment system, digitalisation and data privacy: how citizens emotionally navigate bureaucracy and information systems before they reach a public office. A comparative analysis of Germany's fragmented bureaucracy and Türkiye's centralised e-Devlet system showed how differently societies negotiate trust and security.
works.role: Service design research, UI/UX, data visualisation (team project)
works.context_line: A service design project with the City of Cologne at KISD, 2025.

works.question: How does a personal memory become a collective one?
works.text: An 11-day workshop on İzmir Fair and collective memory. Data visualisation of collected memories, a personal 'memory sentence', and 100 postcards printed with letterpress, linocut and stereotype techniques, exhibited in two municipal exhibitions.

works.title: Abacıoğlu Han
works.question: What can a historic inn tell you if you stay long enough?
works.text: Fieldwork in an İzmir han: observation, interviews, surveys, archival research. A research booklet with texture and typography analysis, HMW questions and a service blueprint, plus a cultural probes box.
works.context_line: Design Methodologies course at Yaşar University, set in İzmir's Kemeraltı.

review.text: This course and project sparked my passion for design methodologies and research-driven approaches. I observed the space extensively, transitioning from research to project implementation, a process I now apply at Bayetav Art, making it an enlightening experience.

works.title: The Fake News Mystery
works.question: What does trustworthy news look like in 2040?
works.text: By 2040, fake news and information bubbles dominate and traditional media is losing relevance. As the innovation team of a media corporation, we reimagined the future of news and a strategy for trustworthy journalism. Our answer: an interactive media literacy detective play kit for children, tangible and digital, distributed through health insurance companies and designed to promote critical thinking through play. Methods included opportunity framing, influence loops, a client journey and a north star metric.
works.role: Team project with Annika, Griet and Philline
works.context_line: Short-term project in Designing Services through a Systemic Perspective, KISD, 2024.

systems.text: eylül learned systems by running them. with ARAMA she coordinated {{giy|GİY}}, an education platform for students; at {{bayetav|BAYETAV Art}} she went from running events to shaping how the whole space worked. now she maps learning paths into a tool at the university of wuppertal: {{lernpfad|Lernpfad-Designer}}.

learning.text: it started with a course in applied drama: learning by doing. at {{giy|GİY}} she designed learning materials and workshops for students, and her thesis {{inner-mechanics|the institute of inner mechanics}} asks how creative education can make room for introspection. today she builds {{lernpfad|Lernpfad-Designer}} at the university of wuppertal.

visual.text: visual communication design was her first language, and she still speaks it every day. since 2019 she has designed identities, publications and websites as a freelancer, and the {{publications|reports and books}} of BAYETAV. her way of working: understanding complexity → structuring ideas → visualizing clarity.

art.text: she makes things by hand, usually with others: letterpress at {{fuar-matbaasi|Fuar Matbaası}}, an installation like {{motif|Motif}}, exhibitions at BAYETAV Art. today her small studio is at the Hidden Agenda Collective, among artists and designers from many fields. at KISD she builds speculative worlds, like {{inner-mechanics|a fictional institute}}.

research.text: cultural studies came first, then fieldwork in places like {{abacioglu|Abacıoğlu Han}}, then a few years of sociology. at KISD she studies how people trust public data in {{cologne|Customer Centers of the Future}} and how education feels from the inside in {{refinding-kisd|Refin(d)ing KISD}}. for her, data is never just technical: it is cultural, emotional and human.

approach.title: how she works
approach.sub: keep scrolling. she walks around a project before she touches it.

steps.label: critical
steps.text: first, she asks why it is like this, and who decided that it should be.

steps.label: speculative
steps.text: then she imagines it otherwise. what if?

steps.label: empathetic
steps.text: she listens to the people it is for, before she draws anything.

steps.label: hands-on
steps.text: she makes it real and tests it with real people, in real places.

steps.label: detail-oriented
steps.text: she goes through every detail, and weaves it back together.

steps.label: honest
steps.text: she shows what happened, including what did not work.

approach.summary: six ways of looking, one project at a time.

cv.bio: Eylem Eylül Acarsoy is a transdisciplinary researcher and designer exploring how identity, expression, and introspection are shaped within societal and institutional structures. With a background in visual communication, ranging from editorial and exhibition design to social media and digital platforms, she brings a holistic and systemic approach to design. Her experience spans managing cultural and educational institutions, facilitating participatory formats, and building archives and communication strategies across art, research, and organizational contexts. She is deeply curious about the ways people connect, learn, and transform together, and often finds herself nourished by the dynamics of community, collaboration, and shared rituals. She asks a lot of questions, laughs a lot, and is happiest when a room full of people starts making something together.
